name: BBQ Chicken Burrito
writer_notes: Source portion was 7 oz chicken; normalized down to 4 oz raw per burrito, which is most of the calorie saving.
Sauce is library S6: blended fat free cottage cheese + 1/3 fat cream cheese + BBQ sauce + lime + smoked paprika + garlic. Cheddar is a separate melt topping.
Fat Free Cottage Cheese is a stub row in ingredients.json (no bid/packaging): not cost-tracked. Flagged.
Bowl cousin: Lean BBQ Chicken and Rice Bowls. This differs as a wrapped burrito built on a blended BBQ crema, not a rice bowl.
intro_html: Sweet, smoky, and honest about its numbers. This one lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein, wrapped in a tortilla that brings 18 grams of fiber for about 5 grams of net carb. The trick is a BBQ crema: blended cottage cheese and a little cream cheese carry the sauce so you get the creamy, saucy feel without a cup of mayo behind it. If you like our Lean BBQ Chicken and Rice Bowls, this is the same flavor you can eat with one hand.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb (1582 g)
Fat Free Cottage Cheese (Great Value): 3 cups (700 g)
1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 5 oz (140 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 3.5 lb: ~$7.78. Buy 4 lbs: $8.92.
Fat Free Cottage Cheese, 3 cups: ~$2.81. Buy 2 24oz tubs: $5.46.
Pantry seasonings (smoked paprika, garlic powder): ~$0.39. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $28.29 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.02 per burrito. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $37.03 across 14 servings, roughly $2.64 per burrito. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $9.43 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $46.46. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: That is about ${{cost_ps}} a burrito (at everyday cost) versus $10 or more for a BBQ chicken bowl at a fast-casual spot. Catch the breast on sale and it slides lower.
shop_smart: Regular BBQ sauce is fine, but read the label. One bottle sauces the whole batch. If you want to shave carbs, the no-sugar-added versions taste nearly identical once they hit the hot chicken.
A little cream cheese goes a long way. You only need part of one 8 ounce brick to make the crema silky, so the rest keeps for bagels or the next batch.

Cottage cheese is the protein trick in the sauce. Blended smooth, nobody knows it is there, and it turns a normally fatty sauce into a lean one. Buy the big tub and you will find other uses for it fast.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cube the chicken breast and cook it in a skillet with the vegetable oil over medium-high heat until it reaches 165F inside.
Turn the heat low, pour in the BBQ sauce, and toss until every piece is coated.
Make the crema: blend the fat free cottage cheese, cream cheese, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and lime juice until smooth.
Fold the crema into the warm BBQ chicken.
Warm the tortillas, then fill each with the BBQ chicken, a scatter of shredded cheddar, and the sliced green onions before you wrap.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total food weight by 14 and scoop the same amount into each tortilla. Every burrito lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

steps: Cube and cook the chicken breast in the vegetable oil until it reaches 165F.
Lower the heat, add the BBQ sauce, and toss to coat.
Blend the fat free cottage cheese, cream cheese, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and lime juice into a smooth crema.
Fold the crema into the BBQ chicken.
Fill warmed tortillas with the chicken, shredded cheddar, and green onions.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 equal burritos.
